summary: State actors, alliances, sanctions, treaties, military posturing, diplomatic moves, and inter-state disputes. The story is the geopolitical action itself, not the market or domestic-policy fallout.
fits_when: primary_entities includes a state, head of state, foreign ministry, defence ministry, alliance body (NATO, EU, ASEAN, G7), or treaty mechanism
primary_geos has at least one country code
fits_poorly_when: primary_entities is mostly companies or markets (use finance)
story is principally about an active military engagement with casualty figures (use conflict)
story is about a domestic regulatory rule change (use policy)

preferred_pattern.describes: named affected population, alliance, or trade lane
labelled map of the named theatre
preferred_pattern.include_when: primary_geos has 2+ countries OR a named region

preferred_pattern.describes: the move itself — what the state actor did
the counterparty response or the trigger
the next scheduled summit, vote, or deadline

notes: Map module is preferred for geopolitics — it grounds the story in space. Skip only if the story is single-country domestic foreign-policy speech.
Quote modules work when 02_evidence has a verbatim line from a head of state or foreign minister; rare from synth — usually gets paraphrased.

asset_hint_policy.map: the workhorse for geopolitics — must be labelled with country / region names
asset_hint_policy.data: use for trade volumes, troop counts, sanctions tonnage, GDP comparisons
asset_hint_policy.mute: default when neither map nor data fits
asset_hint_policy.photo: permitted only when 02_evidence references a specific image source (e.g., a treaty signing photo from a named press pool); never stock

banned_visual_patterns.pattern: Flag fills the frame as primary asset
banned_visual_patterns.why: Reads as nationalism rather than reporting; strips analytical distance
banned_visual_patterns.fix: Flag permitted as L3 chip only; primary asset is map or data

banned_visual_patterns.why: Filler; says nothing about the specific theatre
banned_visual_patterns.fix: Labelled regional map with named places

banned_visual_patterns.pattern: Stock military imagery (fighter jets, troops marching) for a non-conflict story
banned_visual_patterns.why: Implies escalation that the evidence doesn't support
banned_visual_patterns.fix: Map or data; reserve military imagery for stories with explicit military action
Renderer must apply Mapbox labels at the relevant zoom level
Neutral palette; reserve red for explicit casualty / decline figures

lead_with: the official statement from the foreign ministry / head of state office
the treaty / agreement text or readout
the press release of the multilateral body (NATO, UN, EU)
the formal diplomatic note or sanctions list
second_tier: Reuters / AFP / AP wire reporting that quotes the official statement
FT / WSJ / Economist analysis (only when the news is the analysis itself)
treat_with_caution: social media posts unless from verified official accounts
competitor state's framing — quote it, but balance with the issuing state's own statement
must_cite_explicitly: every named diplomatic actor and their title at time of the event

patterns.name: move-actor-place
patterns.example: Tokyo grounded all flights to Sapporo on Tuesday after the magnitude-6.4 earthquake.

patterns.name: treaty-tally
patterns.example: Twelve NATO members signed the joint air-defence pact yesterday in Brussels.

patterns.name: reversal
patterns.shape: <actor> lifted/imposed <action> on <country> for the first time since <date>.
patterns.example: The U.S. lifted the export ban on advanced chips to South Korea for the first time since 2022.

patterns.name: named-readout
patterns.example: President Xi told Chancellor Merz that China rejects 'unilateral tariff measures' in their Tuesday call.

first_4_words_must_contain: a state, capital, or alliance body name (Tokyo, Beijing, NATO, EU)
OR a head-of-state / foreign-minister proper name

good: Tokyo grounded all flights to Sapporo on Tuesday after the magnitude-6.4 earthquake.
Twelve NATO members signed the joint air-defence pact yesterday in Brussels.
The EU froze €1.4 billion in Russian central bank reserves on Wednesday.
bad: Tensions are rising across the Taiwan Strait this week.
Could the new sanctions actually work?
In a provocative move, Beijing has...

L1_rules: include the magnitude when the verb has a number
L2_rules: always include the place when the action has one
always include the time when the action is recent
L3_rules: L3 names the issuing body, not the wire
if only wire reporting available, format as 'Reuters · MOFA briefing'
type_specific_rules: Country names use English exonyms in L1 (Japan not Nippon); endonyms only when more recognisable in target audience.
Treaty names abbreviated only after first mention in script; subtitle L1 may use abbreviation directly (NATO, ASEAN, NAFTA).
Numbers of countries / signatories rendered as numerals ('12' not 'twelve').

module_selection_hints.include_map_when: primary_geos has 2+ countries OR the story names a specific region (Sahel, South China Sea, Donbas, Western Balkans)
module_selection_hints.include_quote_when: 02_evidence.quotes has a verbatim line from a head of state, foreign minister, or alliance secretary-general
module_selection_hints.include_data_when: the story has trade volumes, sanctioned dollar amounts, troop counts, or comparative GDP figures
module_selection_hints.stakes_module_must_name: the affected population (with a number), the threatened trade lane, OR the next scheduled multilateral event

anti_patterns.shape: Hook attributes a move to anonymous officials
anti_patterns.fix: Name the agency or person; if only anonymous sources exist, surface in 01_understanding.unknown_or_disputed

anti_patterns.why: Hedge violation; speculation rendered as forward outlook
anti_patterns.fix: Close anchors on a scheduled summit, vote, or response deadline — not on speculative consequence

anti_patterns.shape: Map asset rendered with no place names overlaid
anti_patterns.why: Reduces map to decoration; render/missing-asset-style failure
anti_patterns.fix: Renderer must apply labels at the relevant zoom level; if no place is named-enough, use data module instead

anti_patterns.pattern: Bilateral commercial dispute classified as geopolitics
anti_patterns.shape: A USTR investigation into one company's tariffs framed as a 'US vs <country>' geopolitical event
anti_patterns.why: Type mismatch; downstream template is wrong
anti_patterns.fix: Reclassify as policy or finance unless state-level instruments are involved

anti_patterns.shape: Module fills frame with a flag
anti_patterns.fix: Flag permitted only as L3 chip
Stakes states what was done and to whom; the audience can judge

anti_patterns.shape: 'Tensions will likely continue in the coming weeks'
anti_patterns.fix: Close anchors on a specific scheduled event: 'The G7 foreign ministers meet October 4 in Hiroshima'

stage_2_extra_checks: verify primary_places resolves at least one specific city or region; vague continental references ('Asia', 'Africa') flag the story for additional sourcing
if a sanctions / trade figure is cited, the source must be the issuing body (Treasury OFAC, EU OJ) or wire that quotes it
stage_5_extra_checks: scan hook + stakes for banned moralisers: aggressive, provocative, belligerent, hostile
verify map module has a label-bearing place name in 01_understanding.where
verify close points at a scheduled date or named event, not 'in coming weeks'
